findings.evidence: The four terms below are the ones a reader meets most often, not the whole vocabulary: Axis 3 also takes SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED and UNMEASURED
findings.issue: The sentence says 'four terms' and then introduces a list that mixes Axis-1 provenance, Axis-2 epistemic status, and Axis-3 measurement status. Although the following paragraph clarifies the axes, the initial enumeration invites the reader to treat ILLUSTRATIVE and HYPOTHESIS as peer measurement-status values.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the lead-in to say 'four frequently used labels from different axes' and keep the axis clarification before listing them, or split the list explicitly by axis.

findings.evidence: A change to the content requires a new build identifier, which invalidates the prior edition and is recorded in the release log — except a dated post-cutoff addendum carried under its own revision identifier and listed in the Appendix addenda row.
findings.issue: The exception clause is hard to parse and appears to allow a content change without invalidating the prior edition when it is a dated addendum. This conflicts with the preceding sentence's categorical rule and leaves unclear whether the addendum is part of the edition or a separate overlay.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite as two sentences: one stating the general rule (content changes require a new build identifier), and one defining the addendum exception precisely, including whether the addendum is part of the edition's content.

findings.evidence: Post-cutoff policy: any model, price or spec that changed after 2026-08-30 is not silently updated in this edition; a later build revalidates the fast-moving claims against current vendor documentation and flags any post-cutoff change separately rather than inheriting the prior value.
findings.issue: The Preface states that post-cutoff changes are 'not silently updated' and are 'flagged separately', but the body contains multiple 2026-10-28 implementation notes and 2026-09-27/2026-11-01 addenda without a consistent inline addendum tag at every point of use. The policy is stated but not uniformly applied.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a uniform inline addendum marker (e.g. 'addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028') at every post-cutoff claim, or move all post-cutoff material to a clearly labeled addendum appendix.

findings.evidence: Preface, 'Evidence boundary' paragraph: "The four terms below are the ones a reader meets most often… Axis 3 also takes SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED and UNMEASURED (all five Axis-3 values are listed in the Axis note below); each term names its axis, and each is the same item as the matching value defined further down this section." The very next parenthetical says: "…HYPOTHESIS (Axis 2, epistemic status) — reasoned but not yet validated (with UNRESOLVED for questions the book leaves open), used where mechanism is argued without measurement."
findings.issue: UNRESOLVED (an Axis-2 epistemic status) is introduced inside a parenthetical attached to the HYPOTHESIS (Axis-2) term within a paragraph that is discussing Axis-3 measurement statuses and claims to list 'all five Axis-3 values' in the Axis note. The Axis note lists five Axis-3 values (ANALYTICAL, SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED, MEASURED, UNMEASURED) but UNRESOLVED is an Axis-2 value, not an Axis-3 value. The paragraph's mixed-parenthetical presentation makes it appear as if UNRESOLVED belongs to Axis 3. The enumeration of 'four terms below' is itself correct (MEASURED, ANALYTICAL, ILLUSTRATIVE, HYPOTHESIS = 4), but the axis attribution of UNRESOLVED in this paragraph is confusing given the explicit warning against mixing axes.
findings.fix_instruction: Move the UNRESOLVED mention so it is clearly within the Axis-2 discussion (or delete it from this parenthetical and rely on the full definition later). Ensure the sentence 'all five Axis-3 values are listed in the Axis note below' is not immediately followed by an Axis-2 value in a parenthetical.

findings.evidence: Preface, §'Hardware is a generic stand-in': "the H100 GPU's 0.989 PFLOPS BF16 dense tensor-core peak and 3.35 TB/s HBM bandwidth, with an 8×H100 host used as the canonical deployment unit — because arithmetic needs concrete anchors."
findings.issue: These are quantitative hardware constants (0.989 PFLOPS, 3.35 TB/s) presented in the Preface without any provenance label. The same values are properly labeled [1P][FACT] in Table 2-2 (page 30) and Table 4-2 (page 74). The Preface states labels run 'from Part I onward' and that front-matter production metadata is exempt — but hardware constants are not production metadata; they are load-bearing quantitative claims. The labeling rule says 'Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair' while also saying 'front-matter and production metadata — a page count, the edition date — are not load-bearing quantitative claims.' Hardware specs used as arithmetic anchors are load-bearing. The Preface itself says 'The rule runs from Part I onward' — but the H100 numbers in the Preface are identical to those the rule covers in Chs. 2 and 4, creating an inconsistency where the same fact is unlabeled here and labeled there.
findings.fix_instruction: Add [1P][FACT] to the H100 BF16 peak and HBM bandwidth figures in the Preface, or explicitly note in the reading-conventions paragraph that hardware constants quoted as exemplars in front matter carry their labels from the chapter where they are load-bearing (Ch. 2/4).

findings.evidence: "The four terms below are the ones a reader meets most often, not the whole vocabulary: Axis 3 also takes SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED and UNMEASURED (all five Axis-3 values are listed in the Axis note below); each term names its axis, and each is the same item as the matching value defined further down this section." Later: "The four terms below are not four values of one axis."
findings.issue: The enumeration invites the exact conflation it later warns against: of the four headlined terms only MEASURED and ANALYTICAL are Axis-3 values, while ILLUSTRATIVE is Axis-1 and HYPOTHESIS is Axis-2, so 'four terms' vs 'five Axis-3 values' can only be reconciled several paragraphs later. The complete Axis-3 vocabulary is buried in a parenthetical rather than presented as the primary list.
findings.fix_instruction: Lead with the five Axis-3 values as a single enumeration, then present the cross-axis highlights (ILLUSTRATIVE, HYPOTHESIS) separately, so the reader never has to infer which of the four terms belong to Axis 3.

findings.evidence: "Where this panel and that paragraph appear to differ, the stricter reading applies: a number is labeled unless that paragraph's exception test clearly covers it" (p. 19) vs "purely illustrative or rhetorical numbers that no later calculation depends on may carry them in the surrounding prose — the exception test is stated in full in the 'Scope of the labeling' paragraph of the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter" (p. 20).
findings.issue: The panel states a default-to-label rule and a tie-breaker ('the stricter reading applies') whose resolution requires the cross-chapter 'Scope of the labeling' paragraph; a reader holding only the Preface cannot determine when the exception test 'clearly covers' a number, and the two default statements point in opposite directions until the later paragraph is consulted.
findings.fix_instruction: Restate the exception test's outcome in one sentence within the panel (or footnote its conclusion), so the stricter-reading rule is operational without the cross-chapter lookup.

findings.evidence: "figure P.1: The architect’s decision loop — the book’s spine... Two loops are drawn, and each is named by the label on its own edge: the inner loop, labelled “re-derive", returns a failed benchmark or TCO validation from “Validate & Defend" to “Design & size"; the outer loop, labelled “iterate", returns from “Commit" to “Understand" when a requirements revision is needed."
findings.issue: Figure vs Caption: The rendered image for Figure P.1 shows the arrows and loops. The caption specifies that the inner loop is labeled 're-derive' and the outer loop 'iterate'. However, the labels are placed in the gaps between stages ('define', 'size', 'justify') and category tags ('inputs', 'work', 'economics', 'decide') clutter the space around the loops, making it ambiguous whether 're-derive' and 'iterate' are visually associated with the arrows or just floating in the same space as the other transition labels.
findings.fix_instruction: Visually separate the loop labels ('re-derive', 'iterate') from the transition labels ('define', 'size', 'justify') to unambiguously associate them with the return arrows, as the caption promises.

findings.evidence: A section reference takes the form § N.M (the thin space after § is optional, so §7.3 and § 7.3 name the same reference), which means Chapter N, Section M — so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4 (Measurement), not Section 1's fourth subsection.
findings.issue: Preface defines § N.M as Chapter N, Section M, but then exempts itself: '§ 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4 (Measurement)' assumes Section 4 exists and is titled Measurement in Ch 1. Body Ch 1 Table of Contents lists Ch 1 as 'It All Starts With the First Token' with no explicit Section 4 label visible in excerpt. Convention not verifiable within provided pages and risks bare § references flagged under mandatory pass 2.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a resolved example that exists in body (e.g., §2.3 or §4.3) and ensure List of Contents includes section numbers/titles so § N.M can be verified to resolve; audit all bare §7 occurrences for missing .M.

findings.evidence: GPU memory, VRAM and HBM are used interchangeably for accelerator-local memory — the same pool under three names: the worked examples write "GPU memory" or "VRAM" for a capacity and "HBM" for the technology, and never mean two different pools by the switch.
findings.issue: Terminology synonym declaration is in Preface only; body Chapter 2 and Chapter 4 repeatedly switch between HBM bandwidth (3.35 TB/s) and GPU memory capacity without re-stating the synonym rule. Per blind spot on GPU memory/VRAM/HBM terminology, a reader entering at Ch 2 may misread HBM as separate pool from VRAM, affecting KV budget vs bandwidth checks.
findings.fix_instruction: Repeat 1-sentence synonym reminder in Chapter 2 §2.1 resource model table footnote and in Chapter 7 intro where capacity vs bandwidth are contrasted.

findings.evidence: The canonical model is a constructed full-MHA teaching geometry (80 layers, hidden size 8192), not a named vendor checkpoint; Ch. 4's "CANONICAL TEACHING MODEL" callout states the intent: GQA/MQA and sparse attention shrink the KV constant several-fold in 2026 production models, so the book's ∼2.62 MB/token is a deliberate upper bound (the derivation: 2 × 80 × 8192 × 2 B = 2,621,440 B = 2.62 MB per token at FP16, one K and one V tensor per layer; grouped-query attention scales that by nKV-heads/nheads).
findings.issue: KV MB/token arithmetic itself recomputes correctly (2*80*8192*2=2,621,440 B ≈2.62 MB), but label scope is ambiguous per blind spot: Preface calls it 'deliberate upper bound' while Chapters 1-2 use the same 2.62 MB/token as KV budget without re-flagging [CANONICAL TEACHING MODEL][ASSUMPTION] vs [1P][FACT]. Risk of treating illustrative bound as measured per-model fact in fleet sizing.
findings.fix_instruction: On every KV budget table (Ch 2 Table 2-2, Ch 4 budget, Appendix A) append provenance tag [CANONICAL TEACHING MODEL][ASSUMPTION][DERIVED] and footnote 'Not a vendor KV-head count; re-derive via nKV-heads/nheads for target model'.

findings.evidence: TTFTe2e = retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill, where tokenization/transfer counts as one combined term. The sum carries no separate "first decode step" term: prefill samples the first token, so a term for that work would count it twice. The canonical 1.2 s budget covers only the two dominant modeled terms (retrieval ∼120 ms + prefill ∼1.08 s); admission/queue and tokenization/transfer sit outside that 1.2 s figure.
findings.issue: TTFT 4-term definition vs 2-term budget restatement is technically consistent (B_other outside budget), but the phrasing 'covers only the two dominant modeled terms' invites misreading the 1.2 s as full TTFT SLO while later chapters test against it as if it were full TTFT. Per blind spot on TTFT 4-term vs 2-term, a stale budget comparison can pass when admission/queue would breach SLO.
findings.fix_instruction: Rename canonical figure to 'TTFT_modelled = retrieval + prefill =1.2 s (budget_prefill ≤1.08 s − B_other)' and require every 'meets 1.2 s' claim to cite B_other measurement status (ANALYTICAL vs MEASURED) per Ch 14 protocol.
